_comment: Castalia-Penta WOUND (CPR3, was CP4a): the TAPE-OUT product configuration -- config/wound.json's peripheral set VERBATIM (QSPI/I3C/NFC/RTC/PWM/OneWire/DMA/I2CTarget/TRNG/EVFAB, cqAfeStubs dropped, fieldPower/PGOOD live, castalia-lqfp100 package) -- PLUS config/penta.json's fifth hart and the CPR3 renumber (numHarts=5, orchestrator=true: HART 0 is the always-on soft `orch_tile` orchestrator in the centre band, keeping the flash/XIP + boot + trap + a0 wiring, and harts 1-4 are the uniform hardened corner tiles, all four power-gateable). This is the config the MCU_castalia physical lineage is built from, so it is the one the penta genus/P&R chain (genus/MCU_WOUND_PENTA, innovus/common/MCU_castalia_penta) consumes. MEMORY MAP v2 rides the knob here too: SH_AW=16, five read-only TCM apertures at 0x20000 + 0x4000*h, extended flash at 0x40000 -- the QSPI/XIP software must use the new flash base. KNOB INTERACTION NOTE: wound sets peripherals.cqAfeStubs=false, so the AFE/EIS stub bank does not exist here and the `shorch` catalog row (which needs the cqAfeStubs tag) is NOT selected; the orchestrator's wound-config coverage is the generic shared-fabric suite at N=5 plus the TCM apertures, which exist on EVERY orchestrator config (that is why CPR4's `shtcm` is the tape-out-config-capable orchestrator test and `shorch` is not). numHarts=5 + dma=true means nMasters = 5 harts + DMA = 6 (MW=3). Build with: make chip CONFIG=config/penta_wound.json ; prove with: make verify CONFIG=config/penta_wound.json
